mbm-2626.clue: I keep the suspicious biscuits separate.
mbm-2626.quote: At our Friday mystery show, we put a biscuit on a plate for each suspect. When someone gets cleared we eat the evidence. One two-part episode left the dentist's biscuit untouched for a week.

mbm-2627.clue: My hook made a fence around a hole.
mbm-2627.quote: I found a moth hole in my favorite cap and crocheted a green ring around it. My nephew said it looked like a golf green. We sewed on one white bead and called it eighteen.

mbm-2628.clue: My first sparring partner was a paper screen.
mbm-2628.quote: I rehearsed my footwork beside a folded screen. If my heel brushed it the paper rustled. My teacher listened from the doorway and smiled the first time we managed a whole quiet minute.

mbm-2629.clue: The spoon marks go round clockwise.
mbm-2629.quote: I threw a bowl for my brother, who stirs his porridge every morning. I carved little ripples in the glaze following his spoon. He turned the bowl round once and said I'd got the tide right.

mbm-2630.clue: I carry the pink pencil on the water.
mbm-2630.quote: My waterproof map case has one bright pink pencil. At low tide I mark the sand bars I can paddle around. At high tide those pink lines are little secret beaches under my boat.

mbm-2631.clue: My aunt taught me to turn a coat inside out.
mbm-2631.quote: When we go to the thrift shop she checks the lining first. I found a plain raincoat with a bright red lining full of cream-colored swallows. That's the only coat I hope the wind catches.

mbm-2632.clue: I let my lunch take the last shot.
mbm-2632.quote: At the mini-golf picnic the groundskeeper challenged me to play the final hole with a hard-boiled egg. It went right of the cup, bumped a stone and came back. I drew a tiny trophy on the shell before I ate it.

mbm-2633.clue: I made the missing saucer first.
mbm-2633.quote: Gran's favorite cup lost its saucer. I traced the tea ring it left on her table and used that circle at the pottery wheel. Now its little green saucer sits exactly where the ring used to be.

mbm-2634.clue: I heard the portrait before I saw it.
mbm-2634.quote: A visitor at the museum was telling her grandson about the big laughing face round the corner. I sketched my guess from her description. My version and the actual portrait look like old cousins.

mbm-2635.clue: I still have to count the yellow stripe.
mbm-2635.quote: At folk dance I learned the turning pattern by counting the yellow stripes on my partner's skirt. Years later I lead the dance myself and my foot still taps when a yellow stripe goes by.

mbm-2636.quote: My park chess partner lost a knight so he carved one from an old bicycle reflector. When it catches the afternoon sun I sacrifice a pawn just to watch it gallop.

mbm-2637.clue: The jam jars needed winter coats.
mbm-2637.quote: I crocheted sleeves for jars of preserves so they wouldn't knock together on the bus. The plum jar got purple, the peach jar gold. Friends asked me what flavor the empty bus seat was.

mbm-2638.clue: My first morning bird was wooden.
mbm-2638.quote: I pointed excitedly at a heron in a pond. Mum let me sketch it for ten minutes before she mentioned the garden shop label. The drawing stays in my journal under birds that held still.

mbm-2639.clue: I let the audience cut the orange.
mbm-2639.quote: I tuck a ribbon into a hollow paper orange and switch it for the one in a basket. When my aunt cut into the paper shell she found the ribbon from her first dance costume. For once she let me keep the secret.

mbm-2640.clue: Our team has a house for its spare key.
mbm-2640.quote: When the curling rink got a new shed I painted four little colored rings around its keyhole. My teammates aim for the button every time they unlock it. Gloves make that harder than it sounds.

mbm-2641.clue: The rain starts in one corner.
mbm-2641.quote: I stitched a cloud in the top corner of my quilt. My niece added drops in blue thread each time she spent the night. It's nearly rained down to the foot of the bed.

mbm-2642.clue: My sunburst has a green ray.
mbm-2642.quote: I ran out of mustard-colored cloth when I made the sunburst. My brother cut a strip from his green concert shirt. He points to that one ray whenever anybody calls it my quilt.

mbm-2643.clue: My game has one polite staircase.
mbm-2643.quote: I wrote a little adventure in which the stairs creak a different note on each step. My mum played the whole tune before she bothered to open the treasure chest upstairs.

mbm-2644.clue: I hike with a pocketful of weather.
mbm-2644.quote: I draw a sun or cloud on a little stone at the trailhead and carry it to lunch. When my friends ask how the morning went I open my hand. They tease me for packing fog.

mbm-2645.clue: I saved a seat for the striped cat.
mbm-2645.quote: I quilted a cushion to match the back of our sofa. A striped scrap in one corner came from the blanket our cat slept on. She found her square before I finished hiding the thread.

mbm-2646.clue: My yellow ball was always late.
mbm-2646.quote: I stuffed my first juggling balls by hand and made the yellow one slightly heavier. I had to throw it earlier to keep the beat. It taught me that things can meet even if they leave at different times.

mbm-2647.clue: My cricket bat has a tide mark.
mbm-2647.quote: We batted on the sand until a wave washed over the spot where I'd set the bat down. I traced the salt line with a pencil. Now the bat knows how high the sea once tried to bowl.

mbm-2648.clue: I met the maker in the gift shop.
mbm-2648.quote: A museum had a whole case of carved toy horses. In the gift shop an old visitor showed me his pocketknife and a horse still half inside its piece of wood. I happily missed the bus home.

mbm-2649.clue: My shopping basket has a bell below the handle.
mbm-2649.quote: I look for old doorbells at street markets. The nicest one came off a bakery. I fixed it to the basket so that every Saturday morning the bakery opens again.

mbm-2650.clue: The first sandwich went to the shark.
mbm-2650.quote: I quilted a picnic wrap just big enough for four sandwiches. My nephew drew teeth along the edge and taught me to fold it like a shark's mouth. Half the fun of lunch is getting it to give the sandwiches back.
